convention: PtYPhiM (mT=sqrt(pt^2+m^2), E=mT*cosh(y), pz=mT*sinh(y)) per T4 ruling 2026-07-24

n_eq_0_branch.note: pfc_mass_GeV == 0.0 exactly and n_pfc_selected == 0, for real PFC rows failing the (vertex==0 & pt>=0.5) selection.

n_eq_1_branch.result: PASS (vacuous on real data; algebraically exact)

reachability_in_real_data.note: No jet in the pT>375 GeV MOD selection ever reduces to n_pfc_selected <= 1, so the n=1 edge condition has no instance in the delivered data.

n_eq_1_branch.algebra: For a single particle E^2-px^2-py^2-pz^2 = mT^2*cosh^2(y) - pt^2 - mT^2*sinh^2(y) = mT^2 - pt^2 = m^2 exactly, so the extractor returns the raw PFC mass in exact arithmetic, as T4 stated.

float64_caveat.cause: Catastrophic cancellation in E^2 - p^2 when m << pt: mass^2 is recovered as a difference of terms of order (mT*cosh y)^2, so the achievable relative precision on m is ~ eps*(E^2+p^2)/m^2. This is a double-precision property of the ruling's own formula, not a deviation from it. The extractor was NOT modified.
float64_caveat.impact_on_delivered_data: NONE. The condition is unreachable (min n_pfc_selected = 4).

precision_in_the_regime_that_actually_oc.test: 3000 real jets (n_pfc_selected >= 2): extractor float64 pfc_mass_GeV vs the same algebra in float80 (numpy longdouble)
precision_in_the_regime_that_actually_oc.note: The delivered pfc_mass_GeV column is numerically clean: the summed-four-vector mass of a real jet is ~10-50 GeV against E ~ few hundred GeV, far from the cancellation regime.
